subject: Digital marketing
label: MARKETING ALIGNMENT
caption_ig:
If your social media link sends people to your homepage, you are wasting your own time.

People don't browse. They click for a specific reason. If they have to search your site to find what you just posted about, they will close the tab.

Link directly to the product, the blog post, or the booking page. No exceptions.

#WebDesign #ConversionRate #SmallBusinessTips #DigitalMarketing #UserExperience
caption_fb:
We spend hours polishing our social media posts, writing newsletters, and setting up ads. But we rarely test what happens after someone actually clicks.

If you run an ad for a specific service, but your website's main headline uses confusing corporate jargon that doesn't match the ad, people assume they are in the wrong place and leave.

Take five minutes today to click through your own active marketing links on your phone. Make sure your website actually delivers on the exact promise your post or email made.
caption_li:
Many small businesses struggle with high bounce rates on their website, assuming it is a design or copy issue. Often, it is simply a broken user journey.

When your external marketing channels (ads, email, social) do not align perfectly with your landing pages, you lose prospect trust instantly. If your Google ad promises one specific solution, but your landing page forces the user to navigate a complex menu to find it, they will bounce.

Your website's job is to finish the conversation your marketing started. Ensure every link drops visitors exactly where they expect to land, with the exact information promised.

slides.title: Where your social media traffic actually goes to die
slides.body: You spend hours creating social posts. But if your link sends people to a generic homepage instead of the specific offer you promised, they close the tab immediately. You paid for a useless click.

slides.title: Stop sending promotion traffic to your homepage
slides.body: If you promote a specific product on Instagram, but link to your homepage, you force users to search for it. Most won't. They will leave. Always link directly to the exact product page.

slides.title: Your Google ads are paying for immediate bounces
slides.body: If your ad promises 'Affordable Bookkeeping' but your website headline says 'Synergistic Financial Solutions', users think they clicked the wrong link. They bounce, and Google still charges you for the click.

slides.title: Your email newsletter is breaking its promises
slides.body: You send an email offering a 'free PDF guide'. But when readers click, they land on a page with three different pop-ups and no clear download button. You just traded trust for frustration.

slides.title: How to audit your own marketing links today
slides.body: Click your own bio links, ad links, and email buttons on your phone. If you have to click more than once to find the promised offer, your website is losing you customers. Fix those paths first.
